simple.meaning: נֶטַע (neṭaʻ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a plant ; collectively, a plantation ; abstractly, a planting.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Job 14:9. The surrounding context includes Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נֶטַע (H5194) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: נֶטַע (neṭaʻ) / H5194 is traced through Job 14:9, Isaiah 5:7, Isaiah 17:10, Isaiah 17:11 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: yet through the scent of water it will bud,
For the vineyard of Yahweh of Armies is the house of Israel,
For you have forgotten the God of your salvation, and have not remembered the rock of your strength. Therefore you plant pleasant plants, and set out foreign seedlings.
In the day of your planting, you hedge it in. In the morning, you make your seed blossom, but the harvest flees away in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow.
